Subject: Sudden latency spikes / increased 5xx rate — noticed after midday deploy

Hi team,

We started seeing sustained P99 latency jumps around 11:30am PT and a sharp uptick in 5xx errors for inference calls to the model you host for us. Error rate climbed from ~0.3% to ~4.8% and throughput dropped by ~20% concurrently. The trend looks like periodic >30s tail latency events and a bunch of request-level timeouts.

No changes on our side — we did not roll anything. Attaching a small graph exported from our monitoring and a sampling of error responses. Can you confirm whether there was a config change or deployment that aligns with these times? This is impacting real-time scoring for a production campaign.

Thanks,
Jared
Principal SRE, PhoenixAI

Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes / increased 5xx rate — investigating

Folks — quick interim diagnostics from the hot lane where PhoenixAI is pinned:

Observations (10:00–10:10 PT):
- KV cache hit ratio dropped from avg 88% to 54% for their tenant; eviction rate spiked at the same time as the latency surge.
- Prefetch subsystem shows a sudden increase in short-lived prefixes (many < 2 tokens) that cause a lot of KV lease churn.
- Batching lanes are imbalanced: priority lane is saturated and starves standard burst lanes. That produces HOL (head-of-line) blocking when a few long-running requests monopolize batch windows.
- No infra deploys targeted at the tenant but a backend kernel update changed kernel scheduling on a subset of machines — that likely changed CPU micro-scheduling and increased prefetch throughput leading to more noisy prefixes.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:05–10:20 PT):
- Reduced prefetch aggressiveness for tenant-level policy and disabled speculative prefetch for 30 minutes. (Attached: kv_config_snapshot.txt and prefetch-trace-20280620.log)
- Temporarily bumped tenant's batch weight to favor standard lanes to reduce HOL exposure.
- Flushed a small set of prefix entries that were hot but low utility.

Impact after changes (10:25 PT):
- Error rate fell to ~1.1% and P99 began trending down; throughput recovered ~12%. Still higher variance than baseline.

Action items:
- Marissa: follow up with a conservative KV eviction/lease policy for Phoenix (prio escalate to platform if needed).
- Rachel: run a replay across synthetic workloads and validate we didn't regress other tenants when reducing prefetch.
- Rishi: coordinate comms with Jared and offer a short credit if we can't fully restore SLA within 4 hours.

Ben
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes / increased 5xx rate — mitigation summary & next steps

Jared — quick update and apology for the impact today. Summary of what happened and what we did:

Summary:
- Root cause (probable): a subtle interaction between kernel-level scheduling tweaks and our prefetch heuristics created a burst of low-value prefixes that drove KV eviction churn and lane imbalance. That produced HOL-like blocking and raised tail latency + 5xxs.
- Immediate mitigations: reduced prefetch aggressiveness, rebalanced batching weights, and flushed noisy prefixes. Those actions brought error rate down to ~0.8% and restored most of your throughput.

Next steps (short window):
- Ben/Platform to apply a conservative tenant-specific eviction/lease profile for Phoenix by end of day.
- Marissa to prepare a rollback plan for the kernel tweak if telemetry shows repeated regressions across other tenants.
- Rachel to run a 3-hour synthetic replay overnight against a canary pool and validate that the prefetch change doesn't harm median latency for other customers.

Compensation & exec escalation: Jonas (cc) — we may need to offer PhoenixAI a one-off credit for the production impact and consider an exec-level outreach if they request it. Jared — we will confirm credits after Ben posts final postmortem.

Please let me know if you want us to schedule a call — otherwise I'll send the postmortem link when ready. Apologies again and thank you for flagging quickly.

—Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
